surfaces.part: stair treads (upper flight, light edge lines at rows 2, 5, 8-9 with darker risers between)

answer.evidence: Terrain tile of a stair cut into a south-facing cliff. Rows 0-5 are a grass cliff-top surface. Rows 2-14 are stair treads, each with a light front-edge line (rows 2, 5, 8-9) followed by darker riser or shadow rows. Brown earth cut-walls flank the stairs in rows 2-14, drawn as vertical faces. Rows 15-31 are a tall dark cobble cliff face, which gives a front face of well over 3 rows. The cliff has a top surface and a front face, so it reads as three-quarter.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a small stair-in-cliff piece, about 2 tiles wide and 1 tile high, so it is a loose match to the grass and paving references. By the measured facts it carries 14 visible tones per tile, against 3 for the grass and 7 for the paving. Near-flat coverage is 0%, the same as both references. By eye, the stair treads are banded light-to-dark, and the stone has speckle and the wooden side posts have grain. No large single-colour areas are visible. Dark edge pixels are 41% near-neutral, so the outline is mixed: brown tints beside the wood, but some grey-black edges, and a little less material-toned than the grass reference (0% neutral). At this size I cannot see much beyond that. Density and shading depth are at or above the references, so I judge it acceptable next to them.
